key_insight: RAG-based type 2 diabetes phenotyping achieved a mean F1-score of 0.9204, with embedding and prompt choices shifting sensitivity, specificity, and token use.
clinical_relevance: Configurable RAG may support EHR-based research cohort identification, but performance priorities must be matched to the phenotyping task.
method: Processed 170,678 clinical notes from 275 ICD-screened patients using GPT-4o.
Benchmarked seven embedding models and 350 embedding–chunk size–retrieval depth combinations on training data.
Evaluated eight optimized configurations with three prompts against ICD codes and PheNorm.
evidence_signal: Across 24 test-set prompt–configuration combinations, mean sensitivity was 0.9019 and specificity was 0.7907; all combinations exceeded ICD-code PPV, and sensitivity significantly exceeded PheNorm.
watch_item: Findings from a small, ICD-screened cohort may not generalize to unselected populations or other conditions.
paper_title: Systematic Benchmarking and Optimization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Clinical Phenotyping: A Type II Diabetes Case Study in an ICD-Screened Cohort
